sanskrit: ārtasvaraṃ tu taṃ bhartur vijñāya sadṛśaṃ vane uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ sītā gaccha jānīhi rāghavam
english: Recognizing that cry of anguish as matching her husband's voice in the forest, Sītā said to Lakṣmaṇa: "Go — find Rāghava."

sanskrit: na hi me jīvitaṃ sthāne hṛdayaṃ vāvatiṣṭhate krośataḥ paramārtasya śrutaḥ śabdo mayā bhṛśam
english: "My life finds no steady ground, nor does my heart hold still, for I have heard with intensity that cry of one in utmost agony."

sanskrit: ākrandamānaṃ tu vane bhrātaraṃ trātum arhasi taṃ kṣipram abhidhāva tvaṃ bhrātaraṃ śaraṇaiṣiṇam
english: "You must save your brother who is crying out in the forest — run swiftly to that brother who is seeking refuge."

sanskrit: rakṣasāṃ vaśam āpannaṃ siṃhānām iva govṛṣam na jagāma tathoktas tu bhrātur ājñāya śāsanam
english: Thus addressed, Lakṣmaṇa did not go, for he knew his brother's command — just as a bull fallen under the power of lions cannot move.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tatas tatra kupitā janakātmajā saumitre mitrarūpeṇa bhrātus tvam asi śatruvat
english: Then the daughter of Janaka, enraged, spoke to him there: "O Saumitrī, you are your brother's enemy disguised as a friend."

sanskrit: yas tvam asyām avasthāyāṃ bhrātaraṃ nābhipadyase icchasi tvaṃ vinaśyantaṃ rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇa matkṛte
english: "You who in this situation do not go to your brother — you desire Rāma's destruction, O Lakṣmaṇa, for my sake."

sanskrit: vyasanaṃ te priyaṃ manye sneho bhrātari nāsti te tena tiṣṭhasi visrabdhas tam apaśyan mahādyutim
english: "I think calamity is dear to you; there is no affection in you for your brother — that is why you stand at ease without even looking for that one of great splendor."

sanskrit: kiṃ hi saṃśayam āpanne tasminn iha mayā bhavet kartavyam iha tiṣṭhantyā yat pradhānas tvam āgataḥ
english: "For what purpose have you come here as the chief one, while I remain here — what could I do for him if he is in peril?"

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇaṃ vaidehīṃ bāṣpaśokapariplutām abravīl lakṣmaṇas trastāṃ sītāṃ mṛgavadhūm iva
english: So speaking, the Vaidehi was overwhelmed with tears of grief; Lakṣmaṇa then addressed Sītā who trembled like a doe.

sanskrit: devi devamanuṣyeṣu gandharveṣu patatriṣu rākṣaseṣu piśāceṣu kiṃnareṣu mṛgeṣu ca
english: "O goddess, among gods, humans, gandharvas, birds, rākṣasas, piśācas, kiṃnaras, and beasts —

sanskrit: dānaveṣu ca ghoreṣu na sa vidyeta śobhane yo rāmaṃ pratiyudhyeta samare vāsavopamam
english: — and even among terrible dānavas, O beautiful one, there exists none who could oppose Rāma in battle, who is the equal of Indra."

sanskrit: avadhyaḥ samare rāmo naivaṃ tvaṃ vaktum arhasi na tvām asmin vane hātum utsahe rāghavaṃ vinā
english: "Rāma cannot be slain in battle; you ought not to speak thus. I do not dare to abandon you in this forest without Rāghava."

sanskrit: anivāryaṃ balaṃ tasya balair balavatām api tribhir lokaiḥ samudyuktaiḥ seśvaraiḥ sāmarair api
english: "His strength is irresistible even by the forces of the mighty, even by all three worlds arrayed together with their lords and with the Maruts."

sanskrit: hṛdayaṃ nirvṛtaṃ te 'stu saṃtāpas tyajyatām ayam āgamiṣyati te bhartā śīghraṃ hatvā mṛgottamam
english: "Let your heart be at peace; abandon this anguish. Your husband will return swiftly, having slain that excellent deer."

sanskrit: na sa tasya svaro vyaktaṃ na kaś cid api daivataḥ gandharvanagaraprakhyā māyā sā tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: "That was not clearly his voice, nor could any deity be harmed. It is the illusion of that demon, resembling a phantom city of the gandharvas."

sanskrit: nyāsabhūtāsi vaidehi nyastā mayi mahātmanā rāmeṇa tvaṃ varārohe na tvāṃ tyaktum ihotsahe
english: "You are a deposit, O Vaidehi, entrusted to me by the great-souled Rāma, O one of lovely limbs; I do not dare to forsake you here."

sanskrit: kṛtavairāś ca kalyāṇi vayam etair niśācaraiḥ kharasya nidhane devi janasthānavadhaṃ prati
english: "We have made enemies of these night-roaming demons, O auspicious one, O goddess, on account of the slaying of Khara and the destruction of the forces at Janasthāna."

sanskrit: rākṣasā vidhinā vāco visṛjanti mahāvane hiṃsāvihārā vaidehi na cintayitum arhasi
english: "Rākṣasas emit voices by their craft in the great forest, O Vaidehi — those whose sport is violence; you ought not to be troubled by this."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇenaivam uktā tu kruddhā saṃraktalocanā abravīt paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ satyavādinam
english: So addressed by Lakṣmaṇa, she grew furious, her eyes reddened, and she spoke harsh words to the truthful Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: anārya karuṇārambha nṛśaṃsa kulapāṃsana ahaṃ tava priyaṃ manye tenaitāni prabhāṣase
english: "O ignoble one, O pretender of compassion, O cruel one, O stain upon your lineage — I think this is what you desire, and that is why you speak thus."

sanskrit: naitac citraṃ sapatneṣu pāpaṃ lakṣmaṇa yad bhavet tvadvidheṣu nṛśaṃseṣu nityaṃ pracchannacāriṣu
english: "It is no wonder that wickedness of this sort should arise among rivals, O Lakṣmaṇa — among cruel men like you who always move in secret."

sanskrit: suduṣṭas tvaṃ vane rāmam ekam eko 'nugacchasi mama hetoḥ praticchannaḥ prayukto bharatena vā
english: "You are utterly corrupt — you follow Rāma alone into the forest, concealing yourself for my sake, or perhaps sent by Bharata."

sanskrit: katham indīvaraśyāmaṃ rāmaṃ padmanibhekṣaṇam upasaṃśritya bhartāraṃ kāmayeyaṃ pṛthag janam
english: "How could I, who have as my husband Rāma — dark as the blue lotus, with eyes like lotus petals — desire another man?"

sanskrit: samakṣaṃ tava saumitre prāṇāṃs tyakṣye na saṃśayaḥ rāmaṃ vinā kṣaṇam api na hi jīvāmi bhūtale
english: "Right before your eyes, O Saumitrī, I will cast off my life — of this there is no doubt; without Rāma I cannot live on this earth even for a moment."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ sītayā somaharṣaṇam abravīl lakṣmaṇaḥ sītāṃ prāñjalir vijitendriyaḥ
english: Thus spoken to harshly by Sītā with words that made the moon shudder, Lakṣmaṇa — who had mastered his senses — joined his palms and said to Sītā:

sanskrit: uttaraṃ notsahe vaktuṃ daivataṃ bhavatī mama vākyam apratirūpaṃ tu na citraṃ strīṣu maithili
english: "I do not dare to give a reply, for you are a deity to me. But words unbecoming — that is no wonder among women, O Maithilī."

sanskrit: svabhāvas tv eṣa nārīṇām eṣu lokeṣu dṛśyate vimuktadharmāś capalās tīkṣṇā bhedakarāḥ striyaḥ
english: "For this is the nature of women as seen in these worlds: they are lawless, fickle, sharp-tongued, and sowers of discord."

sanskrit: upaśṛṇvantu me sarve sākṣibhūtā vanecarāḥ nyāyavādī yathā vākyam ukto 'haṃ paruṣaṃ tvayā
english: "Let all the forest-dwellers hear me as witnesses: harsh words have been spoken to me by you — I who speak only what is right."

sanskrit: dhik tvām adya praṇaśya tvaṃ yan mām evaṃ viśaṅkase strītvād duṣṭasvabhāvena guruvākye vyavasthitam
english: "Shame on you — perish! — for thus suspecting me, who stands firm in the word of my elder, owing to your corrupt womanly nature."

sanskrit: gamiṣye yatra kākutsthaḥ svasti te 'stu varānane rakṣantu tvāṃ viśālākṣi samagrā vanadevatāḥ
english: "I will go where Kākutstha is. May you fare well, O fair-faced one; may all the forest deities protect you, O large-eyed one."

sanskrit: nimittāni hi ghorāṇi yāni prādurbhavanti me api tvāṃ saha rāmeṇa paśyeyaṃ punar āgataḥ
english: "Yet the terrible omens that are appearing before me — may I, upon returning, still see you together with Rāma."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇenaivam uktā tu rudatī janakātmajā pratyuvāca tato vākyaṃ tīvraṃ bāṣpapariplutā
english: So addressed by Lakṣmaṇa, the daughter of Janaka, weeping, then replied with sharp words, overwhelmed with tears.

sanskrit: godāvarīṃ pravekṣyāmi vinā rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇa ābandhiṣye 'tha vā tyakṣye viṣame deham ātmanaḥ
english: "I shall enter the Godāvarī without Rāma, O Lakṣmaṇa, or else I will hang myself — or I will cast off my body from a precipice."

sanskrit: pibāmi vā viṣaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam na tv ahaṃ rāghavād anyaṃ padāpi puruṣaṃ spṛśe
english: "Or I will drink sharp poison, or I will enter fire — but I will never touch, even with a footstep, any man other than Rāghava."

sanskrit: iti lakṣmaṇam ākruśya sītā duḥkhasamanvitā pāṇibhyāṃ rudatī duḥkhād udaraṃ prajaghāna ha
english: Having thus reviled Lakṣmaṇa, Sītā, filled with grief, beat her own belly with her hands while weeping in her sorrow.

sanskrit: tām ārtarūpāṃ vimanā rudantīṃ saumitrir ālokya viśālanetrām āśvāsayām āsa na caiva bhartus taṃ bhrātaraṃ kiṃ cid uvāca sītā
english: Saumitrī, looking upon her who appeared in anguish, downcast, weeping, with wide eyes, tried to reassure her — yet Sītā said not a word more to that brother of her husband.

sanskrit: tatas tu sītām abhivādya lakṣmaṇaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ kiṃ cid abhipraṇamya avekṣamāṇo bahuśaś ca maithilīṃ jagāma rāmasya samīpam ātmavān
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, saluting Sītā with joined palms, bowing slightly, and casting many a backward glance at Maithilī, the self-possessed one departed toward Rāma.

sanskrit: tayā paruṣam uktas tu kupito rāghavānujaḥ sa vikāṅkṣan bhṛśaṃ rāmaṃ pratasthe nacirād iva
english: Spoken to harshly by her, the younger brother of Rāghava, though angered, yearning intensely for Rāma, set out quickly.

sanskrit: tadāsādya daśagrīvaḥ kṣipram antaram āsthitaḥ abhicakrāma vaidehīṃ parivrājakarūpadhṛk
english: At that very moment Daśagrīva, having quickly seized upon the opportunity, approached the Vaidehi bearing the form of a wandering ascetic.

sanskrit: ślakṣṇakāṣāyasaṃvītaḥ śikhī chatrī upānahī vāme cāṃse 'vasajyātha śubhe yaṣṭikamaṇḍalū parivrājakarūpeṇa vaidehīṃ samupāgamat
english: Clad in a smooth saffron robe, wearing a topknot, carrying an umbrella and sandals, and hanging upon his left shoulder the staff and water-pot, he approached the Vaidehi in the guise of a wandering ascetic.

sanskrit: tām āsasādātibalo bhrātṛbhyāṃ rahitāṃ vane rahitāṃ sūryacandrābhyāṃ saṃdhyām iva mahattamaḥ
english: That one of tremendous strength approached her in the forest, bereft of her two protectors, as a great darkness approaches a twilight bereft of the sun and moon.

sanskrit: tām apaśyat tato bālāṃ rājaputrīṃ yaśasvinīm rohiṇīṃ śaśinā hīnāṃ grahavad bhṛśadāruṇaḥ
english: He then beheld that youthful, illustrious princess — as a fierce planet regards Rohiṇī deprived of the Moon.

sanskrit: tam ugraṃ pāpakarmāṇaṃ janasthānaruhā drumāḥ samīkṣya na prakampante na pravāti ca mārutaḥ
english: Seeing that fierce, evil-deeded one, the trees rooted in Janasthāna did not tremble, and the wind did not blow.

sanskrit: śīghrasrotāś ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā vīkṣantaṃ raktalocanam stimitaṃ gantum ārebhe bhayād godāvarī nadī
english: And the swift-flowing Godāvarī river, seeing him with blood-red eyes gazing about, out of fear began to flow sluggishly.

sanskrit: rāmasya tv antaraṃ prepsur daśagrīvas tadantare upatasthe ca vaidehīṃ bhikṣurūpeṇa rāvaṇaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed one, seeking to exploit the gap left by Rāma's absence, during that interval approached the Vaidehi in the form of a mendicant.

sanskrit: abhavyo bhavyarūpeṇa bhartāram anuśocatīm abhyavartata vaidehīṃ citrām iva śanaiścaraḥ
english: The inauspicious one in an auspicious form drew near to the Vaidehi who was lamenting for her husband — as Saturn approaches Citrā.

sanskrit: sa pāpo bhavyarūpeṇa tṛṇaiḥ kūpa ivāvṛtaḥ atiṣṭhat prekṣya vaidehīṃ rāmapatnīṃ yaśasvinīm
english: That evil one, in his auspicious form, covered as a well is covered with grass, stood watching the illustrious Vaidehi, the wife of Rāma.

sanskrit: śubhāṃ ruciradantauṣṭhīṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām āsīnāṃ parṇaśālāyāṃ bāṣpaśokābhipīḍitām
english: Auspicious, with beautiful teeth and lips, with a face like the full moon, seated in the leaf-hut, oppressed by tears and grief —

sanskrit: sa tāṃ padmapalāśākṣīṃ pītakauśeyavāsinīm abhyagacchata vaidehīṃ duṣṭacetā niśācaraḥ
english: — her with lotus-petal eyes and garbed in yellow silk, that Vaidehi was approached by the night-roaming demon of evil mind.

sanskrit: sa manmathaśarāviṣṭo brahmaghoṣam udīrayan abravīt praśritaṃ vākyaṃ rahite rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: Pierced by the arrows of the god of love, uttering sacred Vedic sounds, the lord of rākṣasas spoke courteous words in that secluded place.

sanskrit: tām uttamāṃ trilokānāṃ padmahīnām iva śriyam vibhrājamānāṃ vapuṣā rāvaṇaḥ praśaśaṃsa ha
english: Rāvaṇa praised her who was the foremost among the three worlds, blazing with her beauty like Śrī without her lotus.

sanskrit: kā tvaṃ kāñcanavarṇābhe pītakauśeyavāsini kamalānāṃ śubhāṃ mālāṃ padminīva ca bibhratī
english: "Who are you, glowing like gold, robed in yellow silk, wearing a lovely garland of lotuses like a lotus-pool?"

sanskrit: hrīḥ śrīḥ kīrtiḥ śubhā lakṣmīr apsarā vā śubhānane bhūtir vā tvaṃ varārohe ratir vā svairacāriṇī
english: "Are you Modesty, Prosperity, Fame, the auspicious Lakṣmī, or an apsaras, O fair-faced one? Are you Fortune, O one of lovely limbs, or Rati who roams at will?"

sanskrit: samāḥ śikhariṇaḥ snigdhāḥ pāṇḍurā daśanās tava viśāle vimale netre raktānte kṛṣṇatārake
english: "Your teeth are even, peaked, glossy, and white; your eyes are wide, clear, reddened at the corners, with dark irises."

sanskrit: viśālaṃ jaghanaṃ pīnam ūrū karikaropamau etāv upacitau vṛttau sahitau saṃpragalbhitau
english: "Your hips are wide and full, your thighs are like the trunks of an elephant — firm, round, well-matched, and bold."

sanskrit: pīnonnatamukhau kāntau snigdhatālaphalopamau maṇipravekābharaṇau rucirau te payodharau
english: "Your two breasts are full and high-nippled, lovely, smooth like palm fruits, adorned with choice jewels, beautiful."

sanskrit: cārusmite cārudati cārunetre vilāsini mano harasi me rāme nadīkūlam ivāmbhasā
english: "O beautiful-smiled, beautiful-toothed, beautiful-eyed, graceful one — you steal my mind as a river-bank is taken by water."

sanskrit: karāntamitamadhyāsi sukeśī saṃhatastanī naiva devī na gandharvī na yakṣī na ca kiṃnarī
english: "Your waist is measured by a hand's span, your hair is lovely, your breasts are firm — you are neither goddess, nor gandharva woman, nor yakṣī, nor kiṃnarī."

sanskrit: naivaṃrūpā mayā nārī dṛṣṭapūrvā mahītale iha vāsaś ca kāntāre cittam unmāthayanti me
english: "Never before have I seen a woman of such beauty on the face of this earth; and your dwelling in this thicket stirs my mind."

sanskrit: sā pratikrāma bhadraṃ te na tvaṃ vastum ihārhasi rākṣasānām ayaṃ vāso ghorāṇāṃ kāmarūpiṇām
english: "Turn back — may you fare well; you ought not to dwell here. This is the abode of terrible rākṣasas who take on any form they wish."

sanskrit: prāsādāgryāṇi ramyāṇi nagaropavanāni ca saṃpannāni sugandhīni yuktāny ācarituṃ tvayā
english: "Lofty and delightful palaces, city-gardens — prosperous, fragrant — are fitting for you to inhabit."

sanskrit: varaṃ mālyaṃ varaṃ pānaṃ varaṃ vastraṃ ca śobhane bhartāraṃ ca varaṃ manye tvadyuktam asitekṣaṇe
english: "The finest garlands, the finest drink, the finest garments, O beautiful one — and a husband who is the finest — I consider these fitting for you, O dark-eyed one."

sanskrit: kā tvaṃ bhavasi rudrāṇāṃ marutāṃ vā śucismite vasūnāṃ vā varārohe devatā pratibhāsi me
english: "Who are you among the Rudras, or among the Maruts, O pure-smiling one? Among the Vasus, O one of lovely limbs, you appear to me as a deity."

sanskrit: neha gacchantī gandharvā na devā na ca kiṃnarāḥ rākṣasānām ayaṃ vāsaḥ kathaṃ nu tvam ihāgatā
english: "The gandharvas do not come here, nor the gods, nor the kiṃnaras — this is the abode of rākṣasas. How then have you come here?"

sanskrit: iha śākhāmṛgāḥ siṃhā dvīpivyāghramṛgās tathā ṛkṣās tarakṣavaḥ kaṅkāḥ kathaṃ tebhyo na bibhyase
english: "Here there are monkeys, lions, leopards, tigers, deer, bears, hyenas, and vultures — how are you not afraid of them?"

sanskrit: madānvitānāṃ ghorāṇāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tarasvinām katham ekā mahāraṇye na bibheṣi vanānane
english: "Of terrible, swift-moving elephants in rut — how do you not fear them, alone in this great wilderness, O forest-faced one?"

sanskrit: kāsi kasya kutaś ca tvaṃ kiṃnimittaṃ ca daṇḍakān ekā carasi kalyāṇi ghorān rākṣasasevitān
english: "Who are you, whose are you, and whence do you come? For what reason do you wander alone in the dreadful Daṇḍaka forest, O auspicious one, haunted by rākṣasas?"

sanskrit: iti praśastā vaidehī rāvaṇena durātmanā dvijātiveṣeṇa hi taṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇam āgatam sarvair atithisatkāraiḥ pūjayām āsa maithilī
english: Thus praised by the evil-souled Rāvaṇa — and seeing him as a brahmin guest who had arrived — Maithilī honored that Rāvaṇa who had come with all the courtesies due to a guest.

sanskrit: upānīyāsanaṃ pūrvaṃ pādyenābhinimantrya ca abravīt siddham ity eva tadā taṃ saumyadarśanam
english: First bringing a seat and welcoming him with water for the feet, she then said to that one of pleasant appearance: "Everything is ready."

sanskrit: dvijātiveṣeṇa samīkṣya maithilī tam āgataṃ pātrakusumbhadhāriṇam aśakyam uddveṣṭum upāyadarśanān nyamantrayad brāhmaṇavad yathāgatam
english: Seeing him who had arrived in the garb of a twice-born, bearing bowl and staff — one impossible to dismiss given the appearance he showed — Maithilī invited him in the manner of a brahmin, as he had come.

sanskrit: iyaṃ bṛsī brāhmaṇa kāmam āsyatām idaṃ ca pādyaṃ pratigṛhyatām iti idaṃ ca siddhaṃ vanajātam uttamaṃ tvadartham avyagram ihopabhujyatām
english: "Here is a seat, brahmin, please be seated; and receive this water for the feet. Here too is excellent food of the forest, prepared for you — partake of it here at your leisure."

sanskrit: nimantryamāṇaḥ pratipūrṇabhāṣiṇīṃ narendrapatnīṃ prasamīkṣya maithilīm prahasya tasyā haraṇe dhṛtaṃ manaḥ samarpayām āsa vadhāya rāvaṇaḥ
english: Being thus invited, Rāvaṇa looked at Maithilī, the wife of a king, who spoke with full courtesy, and laughing, he fixed his mind upon her abduction — and thereby upon his own destruction.

sanskrit: tataḥ suveṣaṃ mṛgayā gataṃ patiṃ pratīkṣamāṇā sahalakṣmaṇaṃ tadā nirīkṣamāṇā haritaṃ dadarśa tan mahad vanaṃ naiva tu rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: Then, waiting for her well-attired husband gone hunting, she looked out and saw only that great, green forest — but not Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: rāvaṇena tu vaidehī tadā pṛṣṭā jihīrṣuṇā parivrājakarūpeṇa śaśaṃsātmānam ātmanā
english: Then the Vaidehi, questioned by Rāvaṇa — who desired to abduct her — in the form of a wandering ascetic, declared herself.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaś cātithiś caiṣa anukto hi śapeta mām iti dhyātvā muhūrtaṃ tu sītā vacanam abravīt
english: Reflecting "This is a brahmin and a guest — if left unaddressed he might curse me," Sītā reflected for a moment and then spoke.

sanskrit: duhitā janakasyāhaṃ maithilasya mahātmanaḥ sītā nāmnāsmi bhadraṃ te rāmabhāryā dvijottama
english: "I am the daughter of the great-souled Janaka, king of Mithilā; Sītā is my name — may you fare well — the wife of Rāma, O foremost of twice-born."

sanskrit: saṃvatsaraṃ cādhyuṣitā rāghavasya niveśane bhuñjānā mānuṣān bhogān sarvakāmasamṛddhinī
english: "For a year I dwelt in the household of Rāghava, enjoying human pleasures, fulfilled in every desire."

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃvatsarād ūrdhvaṃ samamanyata me patim abhiṣecayituṃ rāmaṃ sameto rājamantribhiḥ
english: "Then, after a year, my husband, together with the royal ministers, resolved to consecrate Rāma as king."

sanskrit: tasmin saṃbhriyamāṇe tu rāghavasyābhiṣecane kaikeyī nāma bhartāraṃ mamāryā yācate varam
english: "But while the consecration of Rāghava was being prepared, the noble Kaikeyī — so she is named — asked a boon of my father-in-law."

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu kaikeyī śvaśuraṃ sukṛtena me mama pravrājanaṃ bhartur bharatasyābhiṣecanam dvāv ayācata bhartāraṃ satyasaṃdhaṃ nṛpottamam
english: "Kaikeyī, having bound my father-in-law with a former boon, asked of that husband of hers — bound to truth, foremost among kings — two things: my exile and the consecration of Bharata."

sanskrit: nādya bhokṣye na ca svapsye na pāsye 'haṃ kadā cana eṣa me jīvitasyānto rāmo yady abhiṣicyate
english: "'I will not eat today, nor sleep, nor drink at any time — this is the end of my life, if Rāma is consecrated' —

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇāṃ kaikeyīṃ śvaśuro me sa mānadaḥ ayācatārthair anvarthair na ca yācñāṃ cakāra sā
english: — so spoke Kaikeyī; my honorable father-in-law implored her with gifts upon gifts, but she did not withdraw her demand."

sanskrit: mama bhartā mahātejā vayasā pañcaviṃśakaḥ rāmeti prathito loke guṇavān satyavāk śuciḥ viśālākṣo mahābāhuḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
english: "My husband is of great splendor, twenty-five years of age, renowned in the world as Rāma — virtuous, truthful in speech, pure, wide-eyed, long-armed, devoted to the welfare of all beings."

sanskrit: abhiṣekāya tu pituḥ samīpaṃ rāmam āgatam kaikeyī mama bhartāram ity uvāca drutaṃ vacaḥ
english: "When Rāma came to his father's presence for the consecration, Kaikeyī quickly spoke these words to my husband:"

sanskrit: tava pitrā samājñaptaṃ mamedaṃ śṛṇu rāghava bharatāya pradātavyam idaṃ rājyam akaṇṭakam
english: "'Hear this that has been decreed by your father for me, O Rāghava: this kingdom, free of thorns, is to be given to Bharata.'"

sanskrit: tvayā tu khalu vastavyaṃ nava varṣāṇi pañca ca vane pravraja kākutstha pitaraṃ mocayānṛtāt
english: "'And you indeed must dwell in the forest for fourteen years — go forth into exile, O Kākutstha, and free your father from falsehood.'"

sanskrit: tathety uvāca tāṃ rāmaḥ kaikeyīm akutobhayaḥ cakāra tad vacas tasyā mama bhartā dṛḍhavrataḥ
english: "'So be it,' said Rāma to Kaikeyī without any fear; and my husband of firm vows carried out her words."

sanskrit: dadyān na pratigṛhṇīyāt satyabrūyān na cānṛtam etad brāhmaṇa rāmasya vrataṃ dhruvam anuttamam
english: "To give but never receive, to speak truth and never falsehood — this, O brahmin, is Rāma's vow, certain and supreme."

sanskrit: tasya bhrātā tu vaimātro lakṣmaṇo nāma vīryavān rāmasya puruṣavyāghraḥ sahāyaḥ samare 'rihā
english: "His half-brother, named Lakṣmaṇa, is powerful — a tiger among men, Rāma's companion, a slayer of enemies in battle."

sanskrit: sa bhrātā lakṣmaṇo nāma dharmacārī dṛḍhavrataḥ anvagacchad dhanuṣpāṇiḥ pravrajantaṃ mayā saha
english: "That brother named Lakṣmaṇa, a walker of the path of dharma, of firm vow, followed him with bow in hand as he went into exile with me."

sanskrit: te vayaṃ pracyutā rājyāt kaileyyās tu kṛte trayaḥ vicarāma dvijaśreṣṭha vanaṃ gambhīram ojasā
english: "We three, deprived of the kingdom on account of Kaikeyī, wander this deep forest with vigor, O foremost of twice-born."

sanskrit: samāśvasa muhūrtaṃ tu śakyaṃ vastum iha tvayā āgamiṣyati me bhartā vanyam ādāya puṣkalam
english: "Rest here awhile; you may stay here. My husband will come bringing an abundance of forest-produce."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ nāma ca gotraṃ ca kulam ācakṣva tattvataḥ ekaś ca daṇḍakāraṇye kimarthaṃ carasi dvija
english: "And you — tell me truly your name, lineage, and family; and for what purpose do you wander alone in the Daṇḍaka forest, O twice-born?"

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvatyāṃ sītāyāṃ rāmapatnyāṃ mahābalaḥ pratyuvācottaraṃ tīvraṃ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: While Sītā, the wife of Rāma, was speaking thus, the mightily powerful Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, replied sharply.

sanskrit: yena vitrāsitā lokāḥ sadevāsurapannagāḥ ahaṃ sa rāvaṇo nāma sīte rakṣogaṇeśvaraḥ
english: "I am the one by whom the worlds have been terrified — gods, asuras, and serpents together; I am that one called Rāvaṇa, O Sītā, the lord of the host of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: tvāṃ tu kāñcanavarṇābhāṃ dṛṣṭvā kauśeyavāsinīm ratiṃ svakeṣu dāreṣu nādhigacchāmy anindite
english: "Having seen you, golden-hued, clad in silk, I find no pleasure in my own wives, O blameless one."

sanskrit: bahvīnām uttamastrīṇām āhṛtānām itas tataḥ sarvāsām eva bhadraṃ te mamāgramahiṣī bhava
english: "Among the many excellent women brought from here and there — may you fare well — become the chief queen of all of them for me."

sanskrit: laṅkā nāma samudrasya madhye mama mahāpurī sāgareṇa parikṣiptā niviṣṭā girimūrdhani
english: "There is a great city of mine called Laṅkā in the middle of the ocean, surrounded by the sea, situated upon a mountain-peak."

sanskrit: tatra sīte mayā sārdhaṃ vaneṣu vicariṣyasi na cāsyāraṇyavāsasya spṛhayiṣyasi bhāmini
english: "There, O Sītā, you will roam the forests with me; you will no longer long for this life in the wilderness, O passionate one."

sanskrit: pañcadāsyaḥ sahasrāṇi sarvābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ sīte paricariṣyanti bhāryā bhavasi me yadi
english: "Five thousand female attendants, adorned with all ornaments, will serve you, O Sītā, if you become my wife."

sanskrit: rāvaṇenaivam uktā tu kupitā janakātmajā pratyuvācānavadyāṅgī tam anādṛtya rākṣasaṃ
english: Thus addressed by Rāvaṇa, the daughter of Janaka, enraged, her limbs without blemish, disregarding the demon, replied:

sanskrit: mahāgirim ivākampyaṃ mahendrasadṛśaṃ patim mahodadhim ivākṣobhyam ahaṃ rāmam anuvratā
english: "I am devoted to Rāma — my husband immovable as a great mountain, resembling Mahendra, unperturbable as the great ocean."

sanskrit: mahābāhuṃ mahoraskaṃ siṃhavikrāntagāminam nṛsiṃhaṃ siṃhasaṃkāśam ahaṃ rāmam anuvratā
english: "I am devoted to Rāma — long-armed, broad-chested, striding with a lion's prowess, a man-lion, resembling a lion."

sanskrit: pūrṇacandrānanaṃ vīraṃ rājavatsaṃ jitendriyam pṛthukīrtiṃ mahābāhum ahaṃ rāmam anuvratā
english: "I am devoted to Rāma — his face like the full moon, heroic, princely in bearing, master of his senses, of wide fame, long-armed."

sanskrit: tvaṃ punar jambukaḥ siṃhīṃ mām ihecchasi durlabhām nāhaṃ śakyā tvayā spraṣṭum ādityasya prabhā yathā
english: "And you — a jackal desires me here, a lioness beyond reach. I cannot be touched by you, as the sun's radiance cannot be grasped."

sanskrit: pādapān kāñcanān nūnaṃ bahūn paśyasi mandabhāk rāghavasya priyāṃ bhāryāṃ yas tvam icchasi rāvaṇa
english: "You surely see many golden trees, O dull-witted Rāvaṇa — you who desire the beloved wife of Rāghava."

sanskrit: kṣudhitasya ca siṃhasya mṛgaśatros tarasvinaḥ āśīviṣasya vadanād daṃṣṭrām ādātum icchasi
english: "You desire to extract a fang from the mouth of a hungry lion — that swift foe of deer, that venomous serpent."

sanskrit: mandaraṃ parvataśreṣṭhaṃ pāṇinā hartum icchasi kālakūṭaṃ viṣaṃ pītvā svastimān gantum icchasi
english: "You desire to carry off Mandara, the foremost of mountains, with your bare hand; you desire to drink the Kālakūṭa poison and walk away unharmed."

sanskrit: akṣisūcyā pramṛjasi jihvayā leḍhi ca kṣuram rāghavasya priyāṃ bhāryām adhigantuṃ tvam icchasi
english: "You rub your eye with a needle, you lick a razor with your tongue — you who desire to possess the beloved wife of Rāghava."

sanskrit: avasajya śilāṃ kaṇṭhe samudraṃ tartum icchasi sūryā candramasau cobhau prāṇibhyāṃ hartum icchasi yo rāmasya priyāṃ bhāryāṃ pradharṣayitum icchasi
english: "You desire to swim the ocean with a boulder hung about your neck; you desire to snatch both the sun and the moon with your hands — you who desire to violate the beloved wife of Rāma."

sanskrit: agniṃ prajvalitaṃ dṛṣṭvā vastreṇāhartum icchasi kalyāṇa vṛttāṃ rāmasya yo bhāryāṃ hartum icchasi
english: "You desire to carry off a blazing fire with a cloth — you who desire to abduct the virtuous wife of Rāma, O so-called auspicious one."

sanskrit: ayomukhānāṃ śūlānām agre caritum icchasi rāmasya sadṛśīṃ bhāryāṃ yo 'dhigantuṃ tvam icchasi
english: "You desire to walk upon the points of iron-tipped spears — you who desire to possess a wife worthy of Rāma."

sanskrit: yad antaraṃ siṃhaśṛgālayor vane yad antaraṃ syandanikāsamudrayoḥ surāgryasauvīrakayor yad antaraṃ tad antaraṃ dāśarathes tavaiva ca
english: "As great as the difference between a lion and a jackal in the forest; as great as the difference between a rivulet and the ocean; as great as the difference between the finest wine and sour rice-beer — so great is the difference between Daśaratha's son and you."

sanskrit: yad antaraṃ kāñcanasīsalohayor yad antaraṃ candanavāripaṅkayoḥ yad antaraṃ hastibiḍālayor vane tad antaraṃ daśarathes tavaiva ca
english: "As great as the difference between gold and lead; as great as the difference between sandalwood and muddy water; as great as the difference between an elephant and a cat in the forest — so great is the difference between the son of Daśaratha and you."

sanskrit: yad antaraṃ vāyasavainateyayor yad antaraṃ madgumayūrayor api yad antaraṃ sārasagṛdhrayor vane tad antaraṃ dāśarathes tavaiva ca
english: "As great as the difference between a crow and Garuḍa, son of Vinatā; as great as the difference between a grebe and a peacock; as great as the difference between a sāras crane and a vulture in the forest — so great is the difference between the son of Daśaratha and you."

sanskrit: tasmin sahasrākṣasamaprabhāve rāme sthite kārmukabāṇapāṇau hṛtāpi te 'haṃ na jarāṃ gamiṣye vajraṃ yathā makṣikayāvagīrṇam
english: "Even if I were taken by you — while Rāma, equal in might to the thousand-eyed Indra, stands with bow and arrow in hand — I would not decay, as a thunderbolt swallowed by a fly would not decay."

sanskrit: itīva tad vākyam aduṣṭabhāvā sudṛṣṭam uktvā rajanīcaraṃ tam gātraprakampād vyathitā babhūva vātoddhatā sā kadalīva tanvī
english: Having spoken that word with pure heart and clear sight to that night-roaming demon, she — the slender one — trembled from a shuddering of her limbs, like a plantain tree shaken by the wind.

sanskrit: tāṃ vepamānām upalakṣya sītāṃ sa rāvaṇo mṛtyusamaprabhāvaḥ kulaṃ balaṃ nāma ca karma cātmanaḥ samācacakṣe bhayakāraṇārtham
english: Observing Sītā trembling, that Rāvaṇa — equal in power to Death — declared his lineage, his strength, his name, and his deeds, in order to cause her fear.
